findings.location: retail[2] Cisco Systems / CSCO, Where It Breaks
findings.issue: The break test cited Reuters 'Volkswagen expects chip shortage to ease later in 2022' [[n0933]] to assert that Cisco 'still lives with supply constraints'. An automaker's chip outlook does not establish a Cisco-specific supply constraint; the claim overreached its headline.
findings.resolution: Removed n0933 and the unsupported supply-constraint claim. The break test now rests on Cisco's own competing uses of cash: WSJ 'Cisco Made $20 Billion-Plus Takeover Offer for Splunk' [[n1094]] (11 Feb, within the 7-day news window) and Business Insider '13 Companies Cisco Could Buy to Beat Rising Competitors' [[n1116]] (14 Feb), framed modally (a large deal would compete with the buyback for that cash).

findings.location: retail[0] Shopify / SHOP, The Social Signal
findings.issue: The attention evidence was almost entirely Roblox coverage (Forbes, Barron's) plus generic retail items, with nothing showing attention to Shopify itself, and opened with a weak 'vocabulary of the coverage' line.
findings.resolution: Added YCharts '$ARKK, Shopify & Tesla's PE – What's Trending on YCharts?' [[n0946]] (10 Feb, within 7 days; not used by any earlier retail edition), described as exactly as its headline allows. Barron's analyst item [[n0903]] moved to Smart Money View. Entrepreneur, Bloomberg/Saluzzi and AFR items kept.

findings.issue: Bloomberg's Roblox-specific headline phrase 'stock-pop narrative' [[n0143]] was generalised to 'through the pandemic, results days became events where the crowd expected a jump', more than the headline establishes.
findings.resolution: Reworded to 'Bloomberg's phrase for what Roblox lost, the stock-pop narrative', keeping the pull-forward-demand mechanism as the general explanation, and added the exact ARKK card move (-3.20% to 72.87 USD, prior close 2022-02-16) next to the Bloomberg ARKK headline [[n1865]].

findings.location: retail[0] Shopify / SHOP, Smart Money View
findings.issue: Druckenmiller framing ('one of the most closely watched investors', 'rather than averaging down') added colour the 13F headline [[n0777]] does not carry; the Roblox CEO line ended with a stock caution.
findings.resolution: Druckenmiller now attributed to Business Insider and described only as selling before the wipeout; Barron's 'analysts wonder what comes next for the metaverse' [[n0903]] set against the Roblox CEO's monetization defence [[n1199]] so the split is named on both sides; filler cut.

findings.location: retail[1] Digital World Acquisition / DWAC, Where It Breaks
findings.issue: Opening line 'A SPAC trades on the deal, not the app' contradicted the item's own argument that app competition and engagement are the risk.
findings.resolution: Replaced with 'Until the merger closes, DWAC is a shell priced on hope for an app that has not launched', consistent with the October 2021 merger agreement context; Truth Social launch timing stays at Forbes' 'slated to launch next week' [[n1866]] and no launch or App Store outcome is described.

findings.location: retail[3] Gold ETF / GLD, Where It Breaks
findings.issue: 'A close back below 1,843.20 USD/oz would return gold to where it stood before the scare' misdescribed the 20-session reference (19 January), when invasion fears were already present.
findings.resolution: Reworded to 'would erase the month's gain'; opening changed from 'pullback headlines' to 'pullback claim'.

findings.issue: Edits pushed the section to 1,399 words, above the 1,350 ceiling.
findings.resolution: Trimmed filler (repeated cautions, 'the professional split is visible', 'rates add weight to every long-duration growth story') to 1,345 words; lead 724, smaller items 196/199/189; verify PASS.

findings.issue: Checked every cited ID against the 2022-02-17 feed for title, src and published_at, timing, preview-vs-outcome and outlet attribution.
findings.resolution: All 34 IDs resolve. All are stamped 10-16 February (day-granular 08:00), inside the 7-day news / 14-day results windows. Results described are all known before 00:00 UTC on 17 Feb: Shopify (16 Feb pre-market), Roblox (15 Feb after the close), Nvidia, Cisco and DoorDash (16 Feb after the close), FOMC minutes (16 Feb). DoorDash's '24%' is attributed to Reuters and not presented as the card's session move (the card shows DASH -6.80% for the regular session). Walmart, Palantir and Roku results and Intel's investor meeting are not described. No spot-FX numbers. Every number matches the card (instrument, 2022-02-16 session, 1s/5s/20s horizon, units) or a headline cited in the same part.

findings.issue: Possible repeats: Roblox (2022-02-16 smaller item), gold/GDX (2022-02-14 smaller, 2022-02-16 lead invalidation), DWAC (considered in 2, 4, 7 and 8 February notes).
findings.resolution: Roblox appears only as supporting evidence inside a new Shopify lead, with all-new 16 Feb citations (none of the 2022-02-16 Roblox item's evidence is reused). GLD is a material update on new 16 Feb NATO/Atlantic Council evidence, kept secondary. DWAC's first item rests on the new Truth Social screenshot catalyst (Forbes/Newsweek/Bloomberg, 16 Feb). No crypto item. Four distinct narratives: broken pandemic growth, political SPAC lottery ticket, buyback value, war hedge.

scope_limits: Headline-level review only: article bodies are not available, so claims are limited to what titles establish. Only the 2022-02-17 feed, card and exclusions plus strictly earlier retail drafts/notes (2022-02-01 to 2022-02-16) were read; strictly earlier feeds were consulted only to resolve which headlines earlier retail editions had cited (one ID lookup in the 2022-02-14 feed and tools/cited_titles.py over earlier retail drafts), never as evidence; no later-date files, nonretail drafts, specs or other reviews. Publication timestamps are day-granular (08:00 UTC placeholders), so within-day ordering cannot be confirmed from metadata; event timing was checked against the stated guardrails. Merged-report citation caps (four uses) depend on the nonretail component, which was not read.

recommended_exclusions.reason: AP 'US official: Russia adds 7K more troops near Ukraine border' is stamped 2022-02-16 (day-granular) but the US official's briefing it reports may have come after 00:00 UTC on 17 February; not cited in retail, and should not be used anywhere in the 2022-02-17 edition as a pre-cutoff fact.
